questions.question: Which differential identity correctly applies the product rule to a matrix-matrix product $C = AB$?
questions.choice_A: $dC = (dA)B + A(dB)$
questions.choice_B: $dC = A(dA) + (dB)B$
questions.choice_C: $dC = (dA)(dB)$
questions.choice_D: $dC = (dA)B - A(dB)$

questions.question: For a differentiable vector-valued function $y = Ax$ with both $A$ and $x$ depending on parameters, which expression captures the total differential $dy$?
questions.choice_A: $dy = A\,dx$
questions.choice_B: $dy = A\,dx + (dA)\,x$
questions.choice_C: $dy = (dA)\,dx$
questions.choice_D: $dy = (dA)\,x - A\,dx$

questions.question: What is the differential of the transpose $A^\top$ in terms of the differential of $A$?
questions.choice_A: $d(A^\top) = A$
questions.choice_B: $d(A^\top) = - (dA)^\top$
questions.choice_C: $d(A^\top) = (dA)^\top$
questions.choice_D: $d(A^\top) = dA$

questions.question: Which identity is fundamental for turning differentials into gradients using the "trace trick" in matrix calculus?
questions.choice_A: $\mathrm{tr}(AB) = \mathrm{tr}(A)\mathrm{tr}(B)$
questions.choice_B: $\mathrm{tr}(AB) = \mathrm{tr}(BA)$
questions.choice_D: $\mathrm{tr}(A^\top B) = \langle A, B \rangle_F$

questions.question: What is the correct differential identity for the inverse of an invertible matrix $A$?
In reverse-mode automatic differentiation, which practice improves numerical stability when differentiating through a solve operation $x = A^{-1}b$?
questions.choice_A: Explicitly computing $A^{-1}$ and then multiplying by $b$
questions.choice_B: Using a linear solve routine for both forward pass and VJP/JVP computations
questions.choice_C: Replacing $A$ with $A + \epsilon I$ only in the forward pass
questions.choice_D: Applying elementwise clipping to entries of $A^{-1}$

questions.question: Which statement best describes the conditioning of the inverse operation in differentiation?
questions.choice_A: The derivative of inversion always reduces the condition number by a factor of two.
questions.choice_B: If $A$ is well-conditioned, then $A^{-1}$ is ill-conditioned.
questions.choice_C: The sensitivity of $A^{-1}$ to perturbations in $A$ scales with $\kappa(A)$, the condition number of $A$.
questions.choice_D: Ill-conditioning in $A$ does not affect the gradient through $A^{-1}$.

questions.question: For the Cayley transform $Q(A) = (I - A)(I + A)^{-1}$ with $A$ skew-symmetric, which practical requirement is crucial for well-defined differentiation?
questions.choice_A: $A$ must be positive definite.
questions.choice_B: $A$ must be diagonalizable with real eigenvalues.
questions.choice_C: $\|A\|_2$ must be larger than 1.
questions.choice_D: $I + A$ must be nonsingular throughout training.

questions.question: Why is the Cayley transform attractive for orthogonal parameterization in deep networks?
questions.choice_A: It guarantees $Q$ is symmetric positive definite.
questions.choice_B: It maps any matrix to an orthogonal matrix without constraints on $A$.
questions.choice_C: It converts a skew-symmetric parameter into an orthogonal matrix while avoiding explicit orthogonalization.
questions.choice_D: It avoids all numerical issues associated with matrix inversion.

questions.question: When backpropagating through $Q(A) = (I - A)(I + A)^{-1}$, which computational pattern is most efficient for the vector-Jacobian product (VJP)?
questions.choice_A: Materialize the full Jacobian of $Q$ and multiply by the adjoint vector.
questions.choice_B: Reuse the forward-factorization (e.g., LU of $I + A$) to implement multiple linear solves in the VJP.
questions.choice_C: Compute the SVD of $Q$ in every backward pass and differentiate through it.
questions.choice_D: Replace $A$ by its diagonal part to simplify the Jacobian.

questions.question: Which statement about forward-mode vs reverse-mode AD for matrix-valued functions is most accurate?
questions.choice_A: Forward-mode is always more efficient regardless of input/output dimensionality.
questions.choice_B: Reverse-mode is always more efficient for scalar-to-matrix functions.
questions.choice_C: Reverse-mode is typically preferable when the output has low dimension (e.g., scalar loss) and inputs are high-dimensional matrices.
questions.choice_D: Both modes have identical computational cost for any function.

questions.question: Which technique avoids forming Kronecker products when computing matrix derivatives in practice?
questions.choice_A: Vectorizing all matrices and applying identity $\mathrm{vec}(AXB) = (B^\top \otimes A)\mathrm{vec}(X)$ explicitly
questions.choice_B: Using automatic differentiation rules expressed as Jacobian-matrix or vector-Jacobian products implemented via solves
questions.choice_C: Constructing the full Hessian of the matrix function
questions.choice_D: Relying on finite differences for every parameter

questions.question: For the log-determinant $f(A) = \log \det A$ with $A \succ 0$, which differential identity underlies efficient gradient computation?
questions.choice_B: $df = \mathrm{tr}(A\,dA)$
questions.choice_C: $df = \mathrm{tr}(A^{-1} dA)$
questions.choice_D: $df = \mathrm{tr}(A^\top dA)$

questions.question: Which strategy best mitigates numerical issues when differentiating through ill-conditioned symmetric positive definite matrices?
questions.choice_A: Add Tikhonov regularization $A \leftarrow A + \epsilon I$ and reuse Cholesky factors in backward
questions.choice_B: Clip individual entries of $A$ to a fixed range
questions.choice_C: Replace $A$ by its diagonal to improve stability
questions.choice_D: Use single-precision arithmetic while keeping the same solver

questions.question: In implementing a custom VJP for the matrix inverse operation $X = A^{-1}$, what is the correct adjoint update given an upstream matrix $G = \partial \mathcal{L}/\partial X$?
questions.choice_A: Accumulate $\partial \mathcal{L}/\partial A$ with $A^{-\top} G A^{-\top}$
questions.choice_B: Accumulate $\partial \mathcal{L}/\partial A$ with $-A^{-\top} G A^{-\top}$
questions.choice_C: Accumulate $\partial \mathcal{L}/\partial A$ with $-A^{-1} G A^{-1}$
questions.choice_D: Accumulate $\partial \mathcal{L}/\partial A$ with $G$

questions.question: Which of the following is a key advantage of using solves and factorizations (e.g., LU/QR/Cholesky) in AD for matrix operations?
questions.choice_A: They preserve exact orthogonality under floating-point arithmetic.
questions.choice_B: They enable reuse of forward-pass factors to compute gradients efficiently and stably without explicit inverses.
questions.choice_C: They eliminate the need for gradient clipping altogether.
questions.choice_D: They guarantee identical gradients across hardware architectures.

questions.question: In training with orthogonal parameterizations, which clipping method is most aligned with preserving orthogonality while controlling exploding gradients?
questions.choice_A: Elementwise clipping of matrix entries
questions.choice_B: Layer-wise adaptive rate scaling (LARS) on parameters
questions.choice_C: Global gradient norm clipping (e.g., clip by $\ell_2$ norm of all gradients)
questions.choice_D: Clipping the spectral radius of each weight matrix by rescaling its diagonal

questions.question: Which failure mode is most likely when backpropagating through $Q(A) = (I - A)(I + A)^{-1}$ if $A$ approaches $-I$?
questions.choice_A: Non-differentiability due to eigenvalue crossings in $Q$
questions.choice_B: Vanishing gradients because $Q$ becomes the identity matrix
questions.choice_C: Exploding gradients due to $I + A$ becoming nearly singular
questions.choice_D: Loss of skew-symmetry in $A$

questions.question: When designing efficient AD for batched linear algebra, which practice most reduces overhead while maintaining numerical fidelity?
questions.choice_A: Unrolling all batches into a single giant block-diagonal matrix for factorization
questions.choice_B: Using specialized batched factorizations/solves and fusing VJP computations to avoid materializing intermediates
questions.choice_C: Computing gradients by finite differences on each batch element
questions.choice_D: Casting to lower precision only in the backward pass

questions.question: Given $y = A^{-1}b$ and an upstream gradient $g = \partial \mathcal{L}/\partial y$, which reverse-mode update for $b$ is correct and numerically stable?
questions.choice_A: Accumulate $\partial \mathcal{L}/\partial b$ with $A^{-1} g$ using an explicit inverse
questions.choice_B: Accumulate $\partial \mathcal{L}/\partial b$ with the solution of $A^\top x = g$
questions.choice_C: Accumulate $\partial \mathcal{L}/\partial b$ with $-A^{-\top} g$
questions.choice_D: Accumulate $\partial \mathcal{L}/\partial b$ with the solution of $A x = g$

questions.question: Which statement about numerical conditioning and gradient clipping for matrix-valued parameters is most accurate?
questions.choice_A: Gradient clipping fixes ill-conditioning in the forward operator.
questions.choice_B: Preconditioning or parameterization (e.g., via Cholesky or Cayley) addresses conditioning, while gradient clipping controls transient gradient magnitude.
questions.choice_C: Clipping by value is preferred to norm-based clipping for matrix manifolds.
questions.choice_D: Condition number does not affect gradient variance in deep nets.
